$comment: `SpentIdentity.v1` -- the FOURTH binding source `scripts/version_binding_
guard.py` reads, alongside published tags, `CandidateArtifact.v1` receipts
and `CandidateDisposition.v1` entries. Owner and checker: the guard's own
`spent_identity_bindings`. Sensitivity proof:
`tests/architecture/test_version_binding_guard.py`.
## Why a fourth source, and why it is a RECORD rather than a special case
The other three sources all describe a version spent BY AN ARTIFACT: a tag
names installable bytes, a candidate receipt names built bytes, a
disposition names a judgement about built bytes. Two coordinates in this
facility's history are spent with NO artifact to point at:
* `0.3.0a6` -- declared on `main` 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-04 and retired
unbuilt. No wheel, no `CandidateArtifact.v1` receipt, no disposition to
chain from. It is spent by DOCUMENTS: the package `CHANGELOG.md`,
`docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md`, the `poetry.lock` path-package line,
`declared-publication-baseline.json` and the rendered
`deploy/rendered/docker-compose.yml` labels all advertised it while it
was the declared identity. Re-declaring it would recreate `0.3.0a2`'s
two-contracts defect with the documents instead of the bytes.
* `0.4.0a1` -- built ONCE (run 33920058598, artifact 9954731961, from
protected-main source `753a004e7f8dbab034d5d6ca565c680d931a5309`,
built source tree `504bc8f71b62646a5e20a22c41827b20ddd88d33`) and then
drifted: the `CandidateArtifact.v1` receipt never entered this
repository, and `#628`/`#631` moved the facility's importable source
under the unchanged declared version before any receipt was committed.
`tests/architecture/candidate_window_baseline.json` is the build-oracle
record of the same fact; this row is what lets an OFFLINE, no-network
reader (`version_binding_guard.py`) refuse it without querying that
oracle.
Before this file existed, `bindings_for` answered ADMIT for both, on both
purposes, because it had nothing on record to refuse WITH -- not a policy
decision, an absence of evidence. This file is the evidence, entered once
by hand from records Michael has already confirmed (the build-oracle window
baseline and the declared-publication-baseline row), and the guard reads it
the same way it reads a disposition log: by SCHEMA, not by filename, so a
THIRD coordinate of this shape is expressible by appending a row -- to this
file or to a new one -- never by editing `version_binding_guard.py`.
## What a row means, and what it does not authorize
A row records that this repository has NO ordinary lifecycle path back to
the named coordinate: it will never be tagged, will never receive a
`CandidateArtifact.v1` for these exact bytes, and must never be rebuilt or
re-declared. It authorizes nothing -- not a successor allocation, not a
disposition, not committing the drifted receipt after the fact. Those
remain Michael's decisions, exactly as `declared-publication-baseline.json`
already states for `0.4.0a1`.
## The transition discipline -- two directions, both failures (ADR-0018)
A coordinate recorded here can later acquire a REAL lifecycle record --
for instance if Michael authorizes committing the drifted `0.4.0a1` receipt
and a disposition alongside it. When that happens the row for it must be
REMOVED in the SAME change that adds the real record, never left behind and
never deleted early:
* removing the row WITHOUT the real record landing in the same change
reopens the coordinate -- `bindings_for` would then return ADMIT, which
is exactly the defect this file exists to close. Caught by
`test_every_known_spent_identity_is_refused_for_both_purposes`, which
names every row by hand and fails the moment one stops being refused.
* leaving the row in place AFTER a real record already covers the same
`(facility, version)` is the failure the other direction of ADR-0018
names: a ledger that only grows stops describing anything, and two
sources refusing the same coordinate for different stated reasons
is worse than one, not safer. Caught by
`test_no_spent_identity_row_duplicates_an_ordinary_lifecycle_record`.
A count ratchet sits alongside both: `EXPECTED_SPENT_IDENTITY_COUNT` in the
test module must be updated in the same change as any row added or
removed here, so neither direction can drift silently.
